thread.title: Dow Jones Futures: New Trump Tariffs On China Kick In; Alibaba Stock Rises On Earnings

author: ED CARSON
title: Dow Jones Futures: New Trump Tariffs On China Kick In; Alibaba Stock Rises On Earnings

organizations.name: alibaba stock rises on earnings dow jones

text:
Dow Jones futures were little changed Thursday morning, along with S&P 500 futures and Nasdaq futures. The U.S. imposed Trump tariffs on a further $16 billion in Chinese goods, even as China trade talks are underway in Washington. That could be a negative for big U.S. multinationals, such as Dow Jones stocks Boeing ( BA ), United Technologies ( UTX ) and Apple ( AAPL ). Alibaba ( BABA ) rose on booming revenue growth. Meanwhile, Facebook ( FB ) said another four million users may have ad their data misused by a third-party app. That's the latest black eye for the social media giant and and the broader, with Facebook stock, Twitter ( TWTR ) and Snapchat operator Snap ( SNAP ) all struggling
X Dow Jones Futures Today Dow Jones futures were at break-even vs. fair value. S&P 500 futures fell a fraction, Nasdaq futures retreated slightly.
In Wednesday's session, the Nasdaq composite rose 0.4%, but the S&P 500 index lost a fraction and the Dow Jones retreated 0.3%.
Trump Tariffs: China Trade War To Escalate U.S.-China trade talks began on Wednesday and will continue on Thursday. But it's unclear if the trade talks, which don't involve high-level staff, will lead to much. Instead, President Donald Trump is escalating the China trade war. The U.S. slapped Trump tariffs on $16 billion worth of Chinese products on Thursday, with China set to retaliate. The U.S. and China already set tariffs on $34 billion worth of goods, with America mulling Trump tariffs on a further $200 billion.
Thursday's Trump tariffs aren't a surprise, so may not have a huge impact on stock market trading.
Dow Stocks United Technologies, Boeing, Apple United Technologies stock fell 2% to 133.32 in Wednesday's stock market trading , the day's worst-performing Dow Jones stock. Shares rose in the prior four sessions amid hopes for a China trade war truce. United Technologies stock is still close to a 136.76 cup-with-handle buy point .
Boeing stock slid 1.1% to 350.03 on Wednesday, breaking a four-day win streak but holding above its 50-day line. Boeing shares are in a flat base with a 374.58 buy point.
As for Apple stock, the iPhone maker rose 1 cent to 215.05. Shares are trading just below record highs. Apple stock broke out after the July 31 earnings report and has rallied 13% in August.
Alibaba Stock Rises On Earnings Report Alibaba earnings came in at $1.22 a share, up 4% vs. a year before or 1% in renminbi terms. Revenue jumpedto $12.23 billion, a 61% year-over-year surge in local currency and 65% in dollars. Analysts polled by Thomson Reuters had projected profit of $1.21 a share and revenue of $11.83 billion. Alibaba missed some other consensus forecasts, especially in local renminbi terms.
Alibaba stock jumped 4.5% to 185.82 before the open.
Facebook Data Scandal Expands The social media giant said late Wednesday that a further four million Facebook users may have had their data exploited by a third-party app, myPersonality. In a blog post, Facebook said it banned myPersonality , saying the app refused an audit and "because it's clear that they shared information with researchers as well as companies with only limited protections in place."
That comes after some 85 million Facebook users' data was exposed via the Cambridge Analytica scandal. Facebook says it has suspended more than 400 third-party apps since March.
Facebook stock was just before break-even early Thursday after rising 0.6% on Wednesday. Shares plunged 19% on July 26 after Facebook warned of slowing revenue growth and also missing some user growth metrics.
Meanwhile, Twitter stock plunged after the short-message social network reported a decline in users vs. Q1. Twitter is purging fake and suspicious accounts, an effort that may cut reported user levels again in Q3. Twitter stock hasn't made much progress since tumbling following the Q2 earnings report.
Finally, Snapchat operator Snap also reported a first-ever sequential decline in users. Snap stock fell sharply and have continued to slide.
